title.en: Decide positive or negative association by comparing with expectation

say.en: Are literate farmers more likely to use drip irrigation? If literacy made no difference, the share of drip users would be the same among literate and illiterate farmers. In this lesson: Define independence of two attributes.
Decide positive or negative association by comparing with expectation.

body.en: A and B are independent if the proportion of B among the A's equals the proportion of B among the α's, which gives $(AB) = (A)(B)/N$. If $(AB) > (A)(B)/N$ they are positively associated; if $(AB) < (A)(B)/N$, negatively associated (disassociated). Complete *association*: all A's are B's (or all B's are A's); complete disassociation: no A is B.
body.kn: A ಗಳಲ್ಲಿ B ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಮತ್ತು α ಗಳಲ್ಲಿ B ಪ್ರಮಾಣ ಸಮವಾದರೆ A, B ಸ್ವತಂತ್ರ: (AB) = (A)(B)/N. (AB) > (A)(B)/N ಆದರೆ ಧನ ಸಹಯೋಗ; (AB) < (A)(B)/N ಆದರೆ ಋಣ ಸಹಯೋಗ. ಎಲ್ಲ A ಗಳೂ B ಆದರೆ ಸಂಪೂರ್ಣ ಸಹಯೋಗ.

say.en: Observed is greater than expected: positive.
Observed is less than expected: negative.
If A and B were independent, we would expect A times B over N in the A B class. With six hundred, five hundred and one thousand, that is three hundred.
We actually observed three hundred and fifty, more than expected.
Observed above expected means positive association: the two attributes tend to go together.

problem.en: N = 1000, (A) = 600, (B) = 500, (AB) = 350. Are A and B independent?

steps.en: So A and B are positively associated.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. N = 1000, (A) = 600, (B) = 500, (AB) = 350. Are A and B independent?

say.en: Let us work this out together. N equals 1000, A equals 600, B equals 500, AB equals 350. Are A and B independent?
Expected AB equals AB/N equals 600 times 500 over 1000 equals 300.
Observed AB equals 350 is greater than 300.
So A and B are positively associated.
So the answer is Positively associated.

problem.en: Of 400 people, 200 are literate (A) and 100 are employed (B); 50 are literate and employed. Is employment independent of literacy?

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Of 400 people, 200 are literate (A) and 100 are employed (B); 50 are literate and employed. Is employment independent of literacy?

say.en: Let us work this out together. Of 400 people, 200 are literate A and 100 are employed B; 50 are literate and employed. Is employment independent of literacy?
AB/N equals 200 times 100 over 400 equals 50.
Observed AB equals 50.
Equal, so independent.
So the answer is Independent.
